name: Export Los Angeles contractor emails from Houzz to CSV with Apify

nodes.name: Fetch up to five matching profiles
Check email sources and remove duplicate profiles

parameters.content:
## How it works
Build a shortlist of general contractors who publish a business email. The default service area is Los Angeles. Each manual run makes one Apify request for up to five Houzz profiles, filters out incomplete or duplicate records, and exports a ten-column CSV.

## Set up
1. In **Choose the service area**, keep Los Angeles or enter one city and state.
2. In **Fetch up to five matching profiles**, select a Header Auth credential. Use `Authorization` for the name and `Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN` for the value.
3. Click **Execute workflow**. Open **Download shortlist as CSV → Binary → data** to download the file.

The template is free. Apify bills the connected account, with a $0.01 cap per manual run.

### 1. Choose a local market and request five profiles
Enter one city and state, such as `Los Angeles, CA`, in **Choose the service area**. Strict filters keep only general contractors with a published email, even when fewer than five match. [Inspect the default search settings on Apify](https://apify.com/perceptive_city_af7/houzz-professionals-scraper/examples/find-los-angeles-contractors-with-public-emails?utm_source=n8n_workflow&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=houzz_first_buyers&utm_content=la_contractors).

An API error stops the request. If it times out, check your Apify run history before retrying to avoid a second charge.

### 2. Check the shortlist and save a CSV
Skip profiles without both an email and its source, then remove repeated Houzz profiles within this run. Two companies can share one inbox and still appear as separate rows.

Open the final node's **JSON** tab for counts of received, skipped, duplicate and exported profiles. In **Binary → data**, download the CSV. A successful search with no eligible profiles returns only the column headers. A published email may be a general inbox and its deliverability is untested.
